_comment: EPISODE 3, TAKE A, SECOND ATTEMPT (seed 4827; 4824 is the rejected first attempt). Three changes from 4824, and nothing else moves. (1) NO mic_grammar. Words have failed to pin this microphone three times and the third attempt rendered a legible RODE brand mark, so the object comes from the SCENE REFERENCE instead: mic_ref_grammar points the prompt at @Image2 and says nothing else about it, and the run passes --scene-ref refs/scene/sceneref-4820-t5-noface.png, which holds the correct unbranded slim black stick mic on this same London corner. (2) FOUR people, EIGHT shots, two each. That is the pace lever: measured on the takes on disk, seeds 4815 and 4816 both configured four people and eight shots, and the one with the pace grammar (4816) rendered EIGHT shots at a 1.36s median while the two-person takes 4820 and 4824 rendered four at 1.79s and 2.26s. (3) The can grammar is unchanged, reach/payoff included. The ~150 words freed by change 1 are exactly what pays for the two extra people.

product._size_comment: Unchanged from 4824. The can drifted between tallboy and soda scale inside that take, so the absolute size stays and is bound against the hand, which is the only other object in frame at a known size.

product._state_comment: No open_state and no opening_extra: the can grammar REPLACES the whole state sentence. NOTE for the record that seed 4824 rendered this can OPEN despite the clause, the per-shot restatement and a product reference photo that is itself a sealed can. The image channel carried the object and not its state. This is attempt two, unchanged, so that it is tested rather than abandoned on one take.

location._comment: Byte-identical to 4824, and the scene reference is now doing the real work: sceneref-4820-t5-noface.png is this same corner. Naming the city stays, because it is the only prompt-side lever against the drift that put episode 2's third take in New York.
